title: Replacing State Before Drop
goal: Learn how `std::mem::take` enables taking field ownership in `Drop`.

sections.text: In languages like C++ or Java, destructors clean up resources by nulling out references or calling helper methods.

sections.caption: `&mut self` prevents moving `buffer` out.

sections.text: Because `drop` takes `&mut self`, you cannot move non-`Copy` fields out of `self`. The compiler blocks this to keep the struct intact.
To consume or flush a field during drop, replace it with an empty default value using `std::mem::take` or `std::mem::replace`.

sections.caption: `std::mem::take` replaces `buffer` with an empty vector.

sections.text: This leaves `self.buffer` in a valid empty state while giving you full ownership of the original data to process or flush.

explanation: Learn how `std::mem::take` enables taking field ownership in `Drop`.
